chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from 'Uthman ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abi Bakr, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
O Aba Bakr, everything upon which the sun has shone has indeed become tahir.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, as the means by which purification occurs here
key_terms.كُلُّ مَا: everything that; a general expression indicating broad scope
key_terms.يَا أَبَا بَكْرٍ: a direct address to the narrator Abi Bakr

ai.seo_question: Does sunlight purify the ground and similar surfaces in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a legal ruling concerning taharah, stating that what the sun shines upon becomes tahir. In the chapter context, it relates to surfaces such as the earth, mats, and reed mats affected by urine and then dried by the sun.
